answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering works after the fact: agents are grouped by their interaction graph and timing patterns, and each cluster gets one identity weight. A new account whose graph overlaps an existing cluster is merged. Attackers must diversify behavior across many accounts, raising the cost per identity to weeks of genuine activity. A relic of past clusters is kept in a cold vault for retroactive checks; a repeated graph summit across clusters flags the whole set for review, cutting each identity's value.
